sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
hindiTranslation: सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा न किसीके पापकर्मको और न शुभकर्मको ही ग्रहण करता है किन्तु अज्ञानसे ज्ञान ढका हुआ है, उसीसे सब जीव मोहित हो रहे हैं ॥
englishTranslation: The all-pervading one takes neither anyone's wrongdoing nor anyone's good deed. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why living beings are deluded.
essence: Ignorance, not action, is what keeps beings confused.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The divine does not collect anyone's good or bad actions. People get confused because ignorance covers their understanding.
simpleInsight: You are not trapped by what you did, but by what you fail to see.
detailedMeaning: Krishna answers Arjuna on the battlefield, where duty feels impossible and every choice seems stained. He moves the focus from action itself to the ignorance that distorts understanding, showing why people stay confused about responsibility.
modernRelevance: A businessman donates to a temple hoping it will cancel his bad dealings. Krishna says the Lord keeps no such ledger of good and bad deeds; the confusion comes from ignorance covering knowledge.
translationLiteral: नादत्ते (does not take) / कस्यचित् (of anyone) / पापम् (wrongdoing) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सुकृतम् (good deed) / विभुः (the all-pervading one) / अज्ञानेन (by ignorance) / आवृतम् (covered) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / तेन (by that) / मुह्यन्ति (are deluded) / जन्तवः (living beings)
insight: The all-pervading Lord takes no one's sin or merit; ignorance covering knowledge is what deludes beings.

quoteVariants.text: The all-pervading one takes no one’s good or bad deed. Ignorance hides knowledge, and beings are confused.
Ignorance veils knowledge; beings lose their way.
The confusion is not in action. It is in ignorance.
